/-!
# Conjecture 7.39

by J. Mennicke

Let $G = \langle a, b \mid a^p = (ab)^3 = b^2 = (a^{\sigma} b a^{2/\sigma} b)^2 = 1 \rangle$,
where $p$ is a prime and $\sigma$ is an integer not divisible by $p$. The group $PSL_2(p)$
is a factor-group of $G$, so that there is a short exact sequence
$1 \to N \to G \to PSL_2(p) \to 1$. For each $p > 2$ there is $\sigma$ such that $N = 1$,
for example $\sigma = 4$. Let $N^{ab}$ denote the factor-group of $N$ by its commutator
subgroup. It is known that for some $p$ there is $\sigma$ such that $N^{ab}$ is infinite
(for example, for $p = 41$ one can take $\sigma^2 \equiv 2 \pmod{41}$), whereas for some
other $p$ (for example, for $p = 43$) the group $N^{ab}$ is finite for every $\sigma$.

a) Is the set of primes $p$ for which $N^{ab}$ is finite for every $\sigma$ infinite?

b) Is there an arithmetic condition on $\sigma$ which ensures that $N^{ab}$ is finite?

Only part a) is formalised here; part b) asks for a condition rather than for a yes/no answer.

Formalisation notes. Since $a^p = 1$ in $G$, the exponent $2/\sigma$ stands for an integer
$\tau$ with $\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$; the group $G$ does not depend on the choice of
$\tau$, and the statement quantifies over all such $\tau$. The epimorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$
is the natural one, sending $a$ to the class of $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
and $b$ to the class of $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$; $N$ is its kernel.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.name: reduceMod
blocks.text:
/-- The natural homomorphism $SL_2(\mathbb{Z}) \to PSL_2(p)$: reduce the entries modulo $p$
and pass to the quotient by the centre. -/
def reduceMod (p : ℕ) : SL(2, ℤ) →* PSL(2, ZMod p) :=
  (QuotientGroup.mk' _).comp (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)))

blocks.docstring:

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.39».generatorImage

blocks.name: generatorImage
blocks.text:
/-- The images of the generators: $a \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
and $b \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. -/
def generatorImage (p : ℕ) : Generator → PSL(2, ZMod p)
  | .a => reduceMod p ModularGroup.T
  | .b => reduceMod p ModularGroup.S

lemma reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_one {p : ℕ} {A : SL(2, ℤ)}
    (h : (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 1) :
    reduceMod p A = 1 := by
  have hA : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) A = 1 :=
    Subtype.ext (by simpa [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map_apply_coe] using h)

lemma reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one {p : ℕ} {A : SL(2, ℤ)}
    (h : (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = -1) :

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma generatorImage_rels (p : ℕ) (σ τ : ℤ) (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) :
    ∀ r ∈ rels p σ τ, FreeGroup.lift (generatorImage p) r = 1 := by
  have hστ : (σ : ZMod p) * τ = 2 := by
    have := (ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff _ _ _).mpr h
    push_cast at this
    exact this
  simp only [rels, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  rintro r (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl)
  · simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_one
    rw [← zpow_natCast, ModularGroup.coe_T_zpow]
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  · simp only [map_pow, map_mul, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_mul, ← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_T, ModularGroup.coe_S]
  · simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_S]
  · simp only [map_pow, map_mul, map_zpow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_zpow, ← map_zpow, ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_T_zpow,
        ModularGroup.coe_S]
    · linear_combination (↑σ * ↑τ - 1) * hστ
    · linear_combination (-↑σ) * hστ
    · linear_combination (↑τ) * hστ
    · linear_combination (-1 : ZMod p) * hστ

def G.toPSL {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) : G p σ τ →* PSL(2, ZMod p) :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup (generatorImage_rels p σ τ h)
blocks.docstring:
The natural homomorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$, sending $a$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $b$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. It is well defined because
$\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$. It is surjective (so that $PSL_2(p)$ is a factor-group of $G$),
but surjectivity is not needed to define $N$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.39».G.toPSL
justification.why_needed: The natural epimorphism G → PSL₂(p) of the problem, obtained from PresentedGroup.toGroup and the (proved) lemma that the relators map to 1 when σ τ ≡ 2 (mod p).

blocks.name: G.toPSL
blocks.text:
/-- The natural homomorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$, sending $a$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $b$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. It is well defined because
$\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$. It is surjective (so that $PSL_2(p)$ is a factor-group of $G$),
but surjectivity is not needed to define $N$. -/
def G.toPSL {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) : G p σ τ →* PSL(2, ZMod p) :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup (generatorImage_rels p σ τ h)

blocks.code:
def N {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) : Subgroup (G p σ τ) :=
  (G.toPSL h).ker
blocks.docstring: The normal subgroup $N$ of $G$: the kernel of the natural epimorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MonoidHom.ker (Mathlib) — N is defined as (G.toPSL h).ker.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.39».N
justification.why_needed: The kernel N of the natural epimorphism G → PSL₂(p), whose abelianization the problem asks about.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question (answer unknown): Set.Infinite {p prime | ∀ σ : ℤ, ¬ p ∣ σ → Finite (Abelianization N_{p,σ})}, where G_{p,σ} = ⟨a,b | a^p, (ab)^3, b^2, (a^σ b a^{2/σ} b)^2⟩ (via PresentedGroup), 2/σ means an integer τ with σ·τ ≡ 2 (mod p) (well defined since a^p = 1), and N_{p,σ} is the kernel of the natural epimorphism G → PSL₂(p) sending a ↦ ±[[1,1],[0,1]], b ↦ ±[[0,-1],[1,0]] (ab of order 3, trace of a^σ b a^{2/σ} b is στ−2 ≡ 0 so it has order 2) — the map must be fixed explicitly, as N depends on the chosen epimorphism; the preamble facts (σ=4 gives N=1, p=41 infinite, p=43 finite) are background, not posed questions.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state mathematically equivalent, faithful versions of part a): answer(sorry) ↔ {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ∀ σ (p ∤ σ), Finite (Abelianization N_{p,σ})}.Infinite with G_{p,σ} = PresentedGroup ⟨a,b | a^p, (ab)^3, b^2, (a^σ b a^τ b)^2⟩, τ representing 2/σ mod p, PSL₂(p) = Mathlib's PSL(2, ZMod p) = SL(2, ZMod p) ⧸ center, and N the kernel of the map a ↦ ±[[1,1],[0,1]], b ↦ ±[[0,-1],[1,0]]. c07 was chosen because (i) it constructs the homomorphism explicitly via PresentedGroup.toGroup with all four relators proved to die in PSL₂(p) (sorry-free, standard axioms only), so N is literally the kernel of the fixed map and nothing is assumed (unlike c03/c04/c08, which bind the map existentially with an unproved surjectivity conjunct — equivalent since existence/uniqueness/surjectivity are true, but weaker style); (ii) it follows the repo naming convention kourovka.«7.39».parts.a inside namespace Kourovka.«7.39» (c03/c04/c06/c08 use bare parts.a); (iii) it is clean under the library's category/AMS linters (c01 and c06 have untagged helper lemmas and would fail a --wfail build); (iv) the inductive Generator type with constructors a, b makes the relators and generator images maximally readable. c02 and c05 are equally faithful alternatives (Fin 2 generators). My edits: docstring only — the theorem docstring now spells out the fixed map and N^{ab}, and the G.toPSL docstring says 'homomorphism' and notes surjectivity is true but not needed/proved.

claims.decomposer_note: Part b): the deliverable is the description of an arithmetic condition on σ, and no candidate condition is asserted in the statement or background; read literally as a yes/no Prop it is trivially true (e.g. the condition σ ≡ 4 (mod p), p > 2, forces N = 1), so there is no meaningful Prop to state.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. One remark: the notes say "N depends on the chosen epimorphism"; in fact every epimorphism G → PSL₂(p) is the natural one composed with an automorphism of PSL₂(p) (any such map sends a to an element of order p and b to an involution with ab of order 3, and all such generating pairs are conjugate under PGL₂(p) = Aut(PSL₂(p))), so N is canonical. The file nevertheless fixes the map explicitly as the notes prescribe.

where $p$ is a prime and $\sigma$ is an integer not divisible by $p$. The group $PSL_2(p)$
is a factor-group of $G$, so that there is a short exact sequence
$1 \to N \to G \to PSL_2(p) \to 1$. For each $p > 2$ there is $\sigma$ such that $N = 1$,
for example $\sigma = 4$. Let $N^{ab}$ denote the factor-group of $N$ by its commutator
subgroup. It is known that for some $p$ there is $\sigma$ such that $N^{ab}$ is infinite
(for example, for $p = 41$ one can take $\sigma^2 \equiv 2 \pmod{41}$), whereas for some
other $p$ (for example, for $p = 43$) the group $N^{ab}$ is finite for every $\sigma$.

a) Is the set of primes $p$ for which $N^{ab}$ is finite for every $\sigma$ infinite?

b) Is there an arithmetic condition on $\sigma$ which ensures that $N^{ab}$ is finite?

Only part a) is formalised here; part b) asks for a condition rather than for a yes/no answer.

Formalisation notes. Since $a^p = 1$ in $G$, the exponent $2/\sigma$ stands for an integer
$\tau$ with $\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$; the group $G$ does not depend on the choice of
$\tau$, and the statement quantifies over all such $\tau$. The epimorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$
is the natural one, sending $a$ to the class of $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
and $b$ to the class of $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$; $N$ is its kernel.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped MatrixGroups

namespace Kourovka.«7.39»

/-- The two generators $a$ and $b$ of the group $G$. -/
inductive Generator
  | a
  | b

/-- The relators $a^p$, $(ab)^3$, $b^2$ and $(a^{\sigma} b a^{\tau} b)^2$ of the group $G$,
where the integer $\tau$ plays the role of $2/\sigma$, i.e. $\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$. -/
def rels (p : ℕ) (σ τ : ℤ) : Set (FreeGroup Generator) :=
  letI a := FreeGroup.of Generator.a
  letI b := FreeGroup.of Generator.b
  {a ^ p, (a * b) ^ 3, b ^ 2, (a ^ σ * b * a ^ τ * b) ^ 2}

/-- The group $G = \langle a, b \mid a^p = (ab)^3 = b^2 = (a^{\sigma} b a^{\tau} b)^2 = 1 \rangle$,
where $\tau$ plays the role of $2/\sigma$. -/
abbrev G (p : ℕ) (σ τ : ℤ) : Type := PresentedGroup (rels p σ τ)

/-- The natural homomorphism $SL_2(\mathbb{Z}) \to PSL_2(p)$: reduce the entries modulo $p$
and pass to the quotient by the centre. -/
def reduceMod (p : ℕ) : SL(2, ℤ) →* PSL(2, ZMod p) :=
  (QuotientGroup.mk' _).comp (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)))

/-- The images of the generators: $a \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
and $b \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. -/
def generatorImage (p : ℕ) : Generator → PSL(2, ZMod p)
  | .a => reduceMod p ModularGroup.T
  | .b => reduceMod p ModularGroup.S

/-- A matrix in $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ that reduces to the identity modulo $p$ maps to $1$ in
$PSL_2(p)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_one {p : ℕ} {A : SL(2, ℤ)}
    (h : (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 1) :
    reduceMod p A = 1 := by
  have hA : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) A = 1 :=
    Subtype.ext (by simpa [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map_apply_coe] using h)
  simp [reduceMod, hA]

/-- A matrix in $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ that reduces to minus the identity modulo $p$ maps to $1$ in
$PSL_2(p)$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one {p : ℕ} {A : SL(2, ℤ)}
    (h : (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = -1) :
    reduceMod p A = 1 := by
  have hA : (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) A :
      Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (ZMod p)) = -1 := by
    simpa [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map_apply_coe] using h
  simp only [reduceMod, MonoidHom.coe_comp, QuotientGroup.coe_mk', Function.comp_apply]
  rw [QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff, Subgroup.mem_center_iff]
  intro B
  exact Subtype.ext (by simp [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, hA])

/-- If $\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$, then the images of $a$ and $b$ in $PSL_2(p)$ satisfy the
defining relations of $G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma generatorImage_rels (p : ℕ) (σ τ : ℤ) (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) :
    ∀ r ∈ rels p σ τ, FreeGroup.lift (generatorImage p) r = 1 := by
  have hστ : (σ : ZMod p) * τ = 2 := by
    have := (ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff _ _ _).mpr h
    push_cast at this
    exact this
  simp only [rels, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  rintro r (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl)
  · simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_one
    rw [← zpow_natCast, ModularGroup.coe_T_zpow]
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  · simp only [map_pow, map_mul, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_mul, ← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_T, ModularGroup.coe_S]
  · simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_S]
  · simp only [map_pow, map_mul, map_zpow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, generatorImage]
    rw [← map_zpow, ← map_zpow, ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_pow]
    apply reduceMod_eq_one_of_map_eq_neg_one
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [pow_succ, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul, ModularGroup.coe_T_zpow,
        ModularGroup.coe_S]
    · linear_combination (↑σ * ↑τ - 1) * hστ
    · linear_combination (-↑σ) * hστ
    · linear_combination (↑τ) * hστ
    · linear_combination (-1 : ZMod p) * hστ

/-- The natural homomorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$, sending $a$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $b$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. It is well defined because
$\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$. It is surjective (so that $PSL_2(p)$ is a factor-group of $G$),
but surjectivity is not needed to define $N$. -/
def G.toPSL {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) : G p σ τ →* PSL(2, ZMod p) :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup (generatorImage_rels p σ τ h)

/-- The normal subgroup $N$ of $G$: the kernel of the natural epimorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$. -/
def N {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) : Subgroup (G p σ τ) :=
  (G.toPSL h).ker

/-- The natural epimorphism sends $a$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem G.toPSL_of_a {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) :
    G.toPSL h (PresentedGroup.of .a) = reduceMod p ModularGroup.T :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup.of _

/-- The natural epimorphism sends $b$ to the class of
$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem G.toPSL_of_b {p : ℕ} {σ τ : ℤ} (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]) :
    G.toPSL h (PresentedGroup.of .b) = reduceMod p ModularGroup.S :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup.of _

/--
Let $G = \langle a, b \mid a^p = (ab)^3 = b^2 = (a^{\sigma} b a^{2/\sigma} b)^2 = 1 \rangle$,
where $p$ is a prime and $\sigma$ is an integer not divisible by $p$, and let $N$ be the kernel
of the natural epimorphism $G \to PSL_2(p)$,
$a \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$,
$b \mapsto \pm\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Let $N^{ab}$ be the factor-group
of $N$ by its commutator subgroup. Is the set of primes $p$ for which $N^{ab}$ is finite for
every $\sigma$ infinite?

Here $2/\sigma$ stands for any integer $\tau$ with $\sigma \tau \equiv 2 \pmod p$; the group
$G$ and the subgroup $N$ do not depend on this choice since $a^p = 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.39».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ∀ (σ τ : ℤ) (h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]), ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ σ →
      Finite (Abelianization (N h))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.39»

items: The exponent 2/σ is modelled by an integer τ with σ·τ ≡ 2 (mod p) (`σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]`), and the statement quantifies over all such τ. Since a^p = 1 in G, the groups for different valid τ are canonically isomorphic (identity on generators, compatible with the map to PSL₂(p)), so this is equivalent to fixing one τ. For p prime and p ∤ σ such τ always exists, so no vacuity.
The hypothesis `¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ σ` ('σ not divisible by p') is kept explicitly even though it follows from σ τ ≡ 2 (mod p) for odd p; for p = 2 it is not implied, so it is included for faithfulness.

The epimorphism G → PSL₂(p) is fixed explicitly as in the decomposition notes: a ↦ ±[[1,1],[0,1]] (ModularGroup.T reduced mod p), b ↦ ±[[0,-1],[1,0]] (ModularGroup.S reduced mod p). PSL₂(p) is Mathlib's `PSL(2, ZMod p)` = SL(2, ZMod p) ⧸ center. (Remark: every epimorphism G → PSL₂(p) is in fact this one composed with an automorphism of PSL₂(p) — a ↦ order-p element, b ↦ involution with ab of order 3, all such pairs being conjugate under PGL₂(p) — so N is actually independent of the choice; fixing the map explicitly is nevertheless the safest reading.)

The homomorphism `G.toPSL` takes the proof `h : σ * τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]` as an argument, since the fourth relator only maps to 1 under this hypothesis; the proof that all four relators map to 1 is carried out in `generatorImage_rels` (no sorry).
`N^{ab}` is `Abelianization ↥(N h)` and 'finite' is the `Finite` typeclass predicate.
`p.Prime` (Nat.Prime) is part of the set-builder predicate, so the set is a set of primes; `Set.Infinite` expresses 'infinite'. A positive answer (`answer(True)`) means the set is infinite.
Part b) is not formalised (as required by the decomposition table); this is stated in the module docstring.

reviewer_notes: Faithfulness checks performed: (1) 2/σ modelled as any integer τ with σ·τ ≡ 2 [ZMOD p]; verified in Lean that such τ exists for p prime, p ∤ σ (so the inner ∀τ is never vacuous), and since a^p is a relator all such τ give the same normal closure, hence the same G and N. (2) The map a ↦ T=[[1,1],[0,1]], b ↦ S=[[0,-1],[1,0]] kills all relators: a^p ↦ 1, S² = (TS)³ = −I ↦ 1 in PSL, and tr(T^σ S T^τ S) = στ−2 ≡ 0 so its square is −I; all proved in the file. (3) The choice of epimorphism is in fact immaterial for p ≥ 5: any epimorphism sends (b, ab, a) to a (2,3,p)-generating triple with trace triple (0,±1,±2), which is nonsingular in Macbeath's sense and hence unique up to PGL₂(p) = Aut(PSL₂(p)); so N is canonical and fixing the standard map (as the decomposition notes require) loses nothing. (4) p = 2 is not excluded, matching the source ('p is a prime'; only the σ = 4 remark needs p > 2); it affects at most one element of the set, so not infinitude. (5) answer(True) ↔ set infinite = 'yes'; answer(False) = 'no'. (6) Set.Infinite on {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ …} encodes 'the set of primes … is infinite'. Part b) ('is there an arithmetic condition on σ') has no statable Prop and is omitted, as the decomposition table requires; preamble facts (σ = 4 gives N = 1; p = 41 infinite; p = 43 finite) are background and not formalised. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning, including with all FormalConjectures library linter options enabled.
